articles.title: Ontogeny and implantation of the dentition in prismatic enamel-bearing reptiles: Insights from extant uromastycine lizards (Squamata: Agamidae).
articles.authors: Marco Bianchin, Abigail S Tucker, Aaron R H LeBlanc
articles.abstract: Prismatic enamel represents a key evolutionary adaptation in vertebrates and likely evolved independently several times. Beyond mammals, the presence of prismatic enamel among extant vertebrates has been identified within uromastycine lizards (Acrodonta). However, many aspects of their dental ontogeny and histology remain poorly understood. This study provides a comprehensive investigation of the postnatal dental ontogeny and histology of the genera Uromastyx and Saara, using an extensive series of specimens analysed via X-ray micro-computed tomography, hard-tissue histology, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). These comparisons reveal three ontogenetic stages that are associated with a shift in diet. We also provide the first documented evidence of limited, but consistent tooth replacement in the anterior dentary in the genus Uromastyx, challenging the traditional view that this group lacks a mixed pleurodont/acrodont dentition. Our histological results further reveal that the dentition is not strictly acrodont. Newly erupted teeth exhibit pleurodont implantation with a multi-tissue attachment system, subsequently acquiring an acrodont-like appearance through rapid pulp infilling and ankylosis. Furthermore, SEM analysis established that prismatic enamel and a complex tubule network are not only localized to posterior teeth but are a feature of the entire dentition across all ontogenetic stages, from insectivorous juveniles to herbivorous adults. These findings establish uromastycines as a model for understanding the convergent evolution of complex dental tissues and suggest that prismatic enamel may have evolved early in the history of this lineage as a specialized adaptation to arid environments and herbivory.

articles.title: Revisiting the ontogenetic status of the Late Pleistocene human frontal bone from Klasies River Main Site.
articles.authors: Frederick E Grine, Timothy G Bromage, Anton du Plessis et al.
articles.abstract: The ontogenetic status of the Middle Stone Age human frontal bone (SAM-AP 6301) from Klasies River Mouth Main Site is relevant to the interpretation of this fossil's morphology. Some maintain that it represents a modern adult, while others argue that it may be from an archaic juvenile, which could explain its lack of a pronounced supraorbital torus. We employed μCT imaging to investigate the nasofrontal suture and frontal sinus, which were used in previous age assessments. High-resolution replicas of the brow region were examined to document its surface micromorphology with respect to vermiculate pattern development. The nasofrontal suture shows little evidence of fusion either internally or ectocranially, but this only indicates that the specimen is unlikely to have been from an aged adult. The frontal sinus is comparatively small, but its volume can be easily matched among other Late Pleistocene human fossils and recent indigenous populations of southern Africa. The anterior and posterior sinus walls are formed by compact bone, whereas its roof is intermittently porous, possibly reflecting active resorption-pneumatic expansion into the frontal squama-at time of death. This may suggest subadult development, although continued sinus expansion into adulthood cannot be ruled out. The surface of the brow region exhibits at most a slight to moderate vermiculate development, but this also may not necessarily be indicative of age. While the patency of the frontonasal suture and the apparently resorptive nature of the frontal sinus roof seem to be more commensurate with adolescence, the ontogenetic age of the Klasies frontal remains unresolved.

articles.title: When the cure adds to the cost: Skeletal muscle mitochondrial effects of bed rest in elderly.
Cardiomyocyte-derived signalling molecules, 'concerting the orchestra?'.
articles.abstract: The dynamic responses of the heart enable effective organism-level responses to different stimuli. Canonically, the heart's dynamism arises from extrinsic cardiotropic neural and endocrine signalling integrated into intrinsic cardiac regulatory mechanisms. However, it has long been recognised that cardiomyocytes are also sources of signalling molecules that act to modulate both intra-cardiac and extra-cardiac responses. After initial investigations in the 20th century, recent evidence has shed new light on the role of specific populations of cardiomyocytes as putative sources of signalling molecules. In particular, there is evidence supporting these 'signalling cardiomyocyte' subpopulations as sources of catecholamines and acetylcholine - the major autonomic signalling molecules. Our focus is primarily on catecholamines, which we use as the model of the paradigm, given the more extensive evidence base - yet we also discuss more recently proposed and controversial signalling molecules. This review interrogates the evidence supporting and challenging the presence and proposed functional roles of these reported cardiomyocyte-derived signalling molecules. The review then finishes by proposing next steps for investigators in the field to approach major outstanding issues.

articles.title: Dissociated orientation biases of local gamma oscillations and cross-laminar delta-gamma coupling in mouse primary visual cortex.
articles.authors: Baitao Liao, Kehan Chen, Zhengjiang Yang et al.
articles.abstract: Gamma-band neural oscillations are implicated in sensory feature processing, yet their laminar organization and cross-frequency coupling in the mouse primary visual cortex (V1) remain poorly defined. Using linear electrode arrays, we recorded local field potentials and multi-unit activity across cortical layers in lightly anaesthetized adult male C57BL/6 mice during presentation of drifting grating stimuli. We systematically characterize orientation selectivity and phase-amplitude coupling (PAC). Visual stimulation most strongly drove cross-laminar PAC involving L6 delta phase (1-3 Hz) and L4 gamma amplitude (25-75 Hz) (hereafter L6-L4 PAC, where the first layer denotes the source of low-frequency phase and the second layer the source of high-frequency amplitude), with significantly greater coupling strength for L6-L4 PAC than for the reciprocal L4-L6 PAC. Notably, local gamma power exhibited a robust, consistent vertical preference, whereas L6-L4 PAC showed a significant horizontal bias. Dataset-level analyses revealed that the vertical preference of gamma originated from consistent clustering of peak directions around vertical, whereas the horizontal bias of PAC emerged from the accumulation of weak, widely distributed individual deviations. These findings reveal a functional dissociation between local gamma oscillations and cross-laminar PAC in mouse V1: gamma power shows a vertical bias that may carry orientation information, whereas L6-L4 delta-gamma coupling shows a weaker horizontal bias and may reflect a form of cross-laminar temporal co-ordination. KEY POINTS: Visual stimulation drives robust cross-laminar phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) from layer 6 delta-phase (1-3 Hz) to layer 4 gamma-amplitude (25-75 Hz), with significantly stronger coupling than the reverse direction (L4 → L6). Local gamma power (25-75 Hz) exhibits a consistent, depth-invariant preference for vertical orientations across all cortical layers. In contrast, L6 → L4 PAC shows a significant horizontal bias, revealing a functional dissociation between local gamma oscillations and inter-laminar coupling. Single-trial analyses show that gamma's vertical preference arises from tight clustering of peak directions, whereas PAC's horizontal bias emerges from weak, scattered individual deviations summing to a population effect. These findings suggest that local gamma power encodes feature-specific orientation information, while L6 → L4 δ-γ coupling provides a stimulus-engaged, horizontally biased rhythmic scaffold for inter-laminar coordination.

articles.title: Increased CA3 burst activity in Doc2α and Syt7 knockout mice.
articles.authors: Raghava Jagadeesh Salaka, Edwin R Chapman
articles.abstract: The hippocampal cornu ammonis 3 (CA3) subfield is central to associative learning and memory consolidation. CA3 pyramidal neurons execute these functions by generating hypersynchronous bursts that feedforward to the CA1. Extensive recurrent collateral connections within CA3 are crucial for the generation of this burst activity. Double C2-like domain-containing protein α (Doc2α) and synaptotagmin 7 (Syt7) are high-affinity calcium sensors implicated in asynchronous release (AR) of neurotransmitter and in the exocytosis of dense-core vesicles (DCVs). Additionally, Doc2α is a sensor for miniature neurotransmission, whereas Syt7 is involved in synaptic facilitation and synaptic vesicle (SV) replenishment. Both Doc2α and Syt7 are expressed in the hippocampus, but their potential roles in spontaneously bursting networks, like CA3, remain unanswered. Using whole-cell recordings at near physiological conditions (33°C-34°C and 1.2 mM Ca2+) in acute hippocampal slices obtained from juvenile (P15-21) knockout (KO) mice lacking Doc2α, Syt7 or both proteins, we report no changes in spontaneous inhibitory or excitatory postsynaptic current frequency or amplitude in CA1 pyramidal neurons. However, there was a marked increase in burst activity, originating in CA3, in all three KO conditions; this was not due to changes in AR or the intrinsic properties of CA3 pyramidal neurons. We propose that this novel burst phenotype in Doc2α- and Syt7-KO mice is unrelated to changes in neurotransmitter release but might be mediated by changes in neuropeptide release from DCVs in the CA3 subfield or along upstream pathways. Regardless of the underlying mechanisms, this work reveals that both Doc2α and Syt7 act to regulate network activity. KEY POINTS: Hippocampal cornu ammonis 3 (CA3) burst activity is critical for associative learning and memory consolidation. Doc2α and Syt7 are high-affinity Ca2+ sensors with similar kinetic properties and are expressed in the hippocampus. Doc2α and Syt7 support various modes of neurotransmitter release and presynaptic plasticity. Both Doc2α and Syt7 are also involved in the exocytosis of dense-core vesicles in neuroendocrine cells. Loss of Doc2α and Syt7 results in increased CA3 burst activity without changing asynchronous release (AR) or the intrinsic properties of CA3 neurons. Our results suggest a novel role for Doc2α and Syt7 in regulating CA3 burst activity.

articles.title: Intercellular crosstalk and functional heterogeneity of hepatic stellate cells: A translational framework for chronic liver disease.
articles.authors: Olga Martínez-Arroyo, Mireia Sastre-Navarro, Juan V Esplugues et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver diseases are a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with hepatic fibrosis representing the common pathological pathway that can lead to cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma. Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are the principal source of myofibroblasts during liver fibrogenesis and have therefore emerged as central therapeutic targets. However, recent advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial omics and lineage-tracing approaches have fundamentally revised the traditional view of HSC activation as a uniform process. Instead, HSCs comprise a spectrum of phenotypically and functionally distinct states that dynamically evolve in response to chronic liver injury and differ in their contributions to extracellular matrix deposition, inflammation, immune regulation, vascular remodelling and tissue repair. During disease progression, HSCs integrate biochemical, metabolic and biomechanical cues derived from injured hepatocytes, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, immune cells and the extracellular matrix, while simultaneously reshaping the hepatic microenvironment through reciprocal intercellular communication mediated by soluble factors, extracellular vesicles, direct cell-cell interactions and matrix-derived signals. This bidirectional crosstalk underlies both fibrosis progression and its potential regression, highlighting HSC plasticity as a defining feature of chronic liver disease. In this review, we discuss the emerging concepts of HSC phenotypic heterogeneity and intercellular communication, summarizing the molecular mechanisms that govern HSC state transitions and their interactions within the hepatic niche. Finally, we examine how these discoveries are transforming current approaches to precision anti-fibrotic therapies, providing a translational framework for the treatment of chronic liver diseases.

articles.title: Reduced spike adaptation in RHEB/mTORC1-hyperactive excitatory neurons influences network hyperactivity.
articles.authors: Anouk M Heuvelmans, Stefan G J Lip, Mario Negrello et al.
articles.abstract: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) pathway plays a crucial role in structural brain development by regulating cell growth, metabolism and other cellular processes. Hyperactivation of this pathway causes refractory epilepsy and enhanced network activity through increased synaptic connectivity. However, patch-clamp recordings of neurons in which the mTOR pathway is hyperactive revealed reduced intrinsic excitability. To unravel the mechanism underlying this paradoxical finding, we combine whole-cell recordings from dissociated murine hippocampal neurons overexpressing the gain-of-function Ras-homolog enriched in brain (RHEB)-p.P37L mutation, with an in silico model to connect cellular changes to network dynamics. We found an increased rheobase, decreased depolarization-induced excitability and increased afterhyperpolarization current in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, confirming hypo-excitability. Further characterization of spike-trains revealed a lack of adaptation in these neurons, enabling neurons to reach shorter interspike intervals in response to higher current injections. We built a computational model of the neurons that reproduces the electrophysiological parameters we measured. This model revealed the interaction between the afterhyperpolarization current and voltage-dependent refractory mechanisms as a potential cause for the reduction in spike adaptation. Network simulation revealed how passive properties, afterhyperpolarization current, and synaptic connectivity contribute to aberrant network activity, suggesting the altered passive properties in RHEB-p.P37L neurons as a cause of reduced burst rhythmicity on network level. Our findings indicate that, in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, excitability is regulated in a state-dependent manner, where baseline hypo-excitability coexists with poor adaptation, promoting high-frequency firing in high-input states. Based on our results, we propose that, in addition to altered synaptic connectivity, differences in state-dependent neuronal excitability underlie mTOR-hyperactivity-induced disruptions of network activity. KEY POINTS: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) pathway is essential for brain development, and hyperactivation of the pathway causes refractory epilepsy and increased neuronal network activity. Neurons with induced mTORC1-hyperactivity display intrinsic hypo-excitability at the single-cell level but exhibit stronger synaptic connectivity in networks than controls. Single-cell recordings from murine primary hippocampal neurons expressing the gain-of-function Ras-homolog enriched in brain (RHEB)-p.P37L mutation reveal increased afterhyperpolarization currents and a marked reduction in spike-frequency adaptation, allowing neurons to fire at shorter interspike intervals during strong current injection. A biophysically constrained computational neuron model recapitulating the biological single-cell intrinsic properties reproduced faster firing in response to strong current injection, and revealed how passive properties, afterhyperpolarization and synaptic connectivity contribute to aberrant network activity. The findings demonstrate state-dependent regulation of excitability in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, where baseline hypo-excitability coexists with impaired adaptation and high-frequency firing, suggesting that altered intrinsic excitability, in addition to increased synaptic connectivity, contributes to mTOR-driven network dysfunction.

articles.title: Effect of ageing on human skeletal muscle nitrate and nitrite metabolism.
articles.authors: Raghini Rajaram, Matthew I Black, Chenguang Wei et al.
articles.abstract: Ageing-associated impairment in cardiovascular function is hallmarked by decreased endogenous nitric oxide (NO) production via NO synthase (NOS) activity. Nitrate (NO3 -) in mammalian skeletal muscle may provide a substrate for an alternative NO3 --nitrite (NO2 -)-NO pathway. Here, we report the effect of ageing on NO3 - storage and metabolism in human skeletal muscle. We evaluated skeletal muscle [NO3 -] and [NO2 -], and the mRNA and protein expression of NO3 - and NO2 - transporting (sialin, CLC1) and reducing (XOR) proteins in young and older humans. Nineteen young (18-30 years) and 19 older (60-80 years) healthy adults provided blood and muscle samples without ingestion of dietary NO3 - (CON) and 3 h after a bolus ingestion of dietary NO3 -. Compared with young adults, the skeletal muscle of older adults had greater [NO3 -] (86.9 ± 38.2 vs. 64.3 ± 23.1 nmol g-1, P = 0.0334) and [NO2 -] (1.2 ± 0.4 vs. 0.8 ± 0.2 nmol g-1, P < 0.001) under the CON condition, and greater [NO3 -] (156.5 ± 50.6 vs. 122.7 ± 38.1 nmol g-1, P = 0.0258) but not [NO2 -] (1.3 ± 0.4 vs. 1.3 ± 0.6 nmol g-1, P = 0.808) post-NO3 - ingestion. The expression of sialin, CLC1 and XOR proteins was not different between age groups although there was evidence of deficiencies in the translation efficiency and protein stability of XOR, post-NO3 - ingestion, in the older adults. Muscle NO3 - uptake was unaffected by age, and older adults had equivalent or better NO3 - to NO2 - reduction efficiency compared with young adults. These results suggest that the NO3 --NO2 --NO pathway may mitigate lowered NO production from the NOS pathway in healthy older adults. KEY POINTS: Nitrate (NO3 -) in mammalian skeletal muscle may provide a substrate for the NO3 --nitrite (NO2 -)-nitric oxide (NO) pathway when endogenous NO production via NO synthase (NOS) activity is adversely affected by age. We show that skeletal muscle of older adults has greater baseline [NO3 -] and [NO2 -], as well as a greater [NO3 -] following bolus dietary NO3 - ingestion, compared with young adults. The expression of NO3 - transporting and reducing proteins was unaffected by age, but the translation efficiency of xanthine oxidoreductase was reduced post-NO3 - ingestion in older adults. Muscle NO3 - uptake was unaffected by age, and older adults had equivalent or better capacity for NO3 - to NO2 - reduction compared with young adults. The NO3 --NO2 --NO pathway has the potential to mitigate lowered NO production from the NOS pathway in healthy older adults.

articles.title: WM-S25: Validation of heated-hand venous arterialization at sea level and high altitude.
articles.authors: Jessica N Kenney, Ibrahim A Wafai, Brooke R Shepley et al.
articles.abstract: Arterial blood sampling remains the gold standard for blood gas and acid-base analysis; however, it can be logistically challenging in research settings, especially during field research. In this study, we evaluated the validity of arterializing venous blood in the hand through 25 min of warm (45°C) water hand immersion, in comparison to direct arterial (brachial) sampling in healthy adults (age range 20-35 years, mean 24 years) at both sea level (334 m a.s.l., n = 15) and high altitude (3800 m a.s.l., n = 11). Agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analyses. For the primary analysis of P O 2 , equivalence testing was also performed with a predefined margin of ±5 mmHg. Secondary analyses included P C O 2 , oxygen saturation, glucose, lactate, pH and HCO3 -. At sea level, hand heating reduced the mean bias for arterial-venous P O 2 from -20.85 mmHg [unheated 95% limits of agreement (LOA): -38.72 to -2.97 mmHg] to -7.99 mmHg (heated 95% LOA: -26.68 to 10.71 mmHg). At high altitude, hand heating reduced the mean bias for arterial-venous P O 2 from -5.99 mmHg (unheated 95% LOA: -11.82 to -0.16 mmHg) to -0.98 mmHg (heated 95% LOA: -3.60 to 1.63 mmHg). Equivalence testing demonstrated that heated venous P O 2 was equivalent to arterial P O 2 only at high altitude, with no equivalence observed in any other conditions. Agreement for P C O 2 , pH, HCO3 -, glucose and lactate was generally good irrespective of hand heating or elevation, whereas heating improved agreement for oxygen saturation at both elevations. These findings support heated-hand venous arterialization as a practical alternative to arterial sampling for assessment of arterial P O 2 during high-altitude research.

articles.title: Myoglobin-dependent regulation of mitochondrial bioenergetics and glucose metabolism in murine C2C12 skeletal muscle myotubes.
articles.authors: Dipendra Bhandari, Michael L Blackburn, Sean H Adams et al.
articles.abstract: Lactate (LAC) accumulates in skeletal muscle when production surpasses utilization and tissue export during exercise. Recent biochemical studies have revealed that increasing LAC concentrations reduce oxygen (O2) binding to equine skeletal muscle myoglobin (Mb). To determine whether LAC-Mb associations affect cellular metabolism, we treated three variants of the C2C12 mouse skeletal muscle myotubes - Mb wild-type (MbWT), Mb knockout (MbKO) and Mb empty vector (MbEV) - with varying concentrations of sodium l-lactate (1.8-8.0 mM) for 3-24 h to assess net LAC uptake, net glucose (GLU) uptake and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Intracellular LAC levels increased in all LAC-treated Mb genotype variants but not in control cells. After 24 h, net GLU uptake was significantly higher in MbKO cells than in MbWT or MbEV cells. At 6 h, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation contributed ∼70% of total ATP production in LAC-treated MbWT and MbEV cells. However, at 24 h, a higher (∼57%-67%) contribution of glycolysis-derived ATP was recorded. Total ATP production was significantly lower (∼35%) in MbKO cells at both 6 and 24 h, largely due to lower glycolysis-derived ATP production (∼26%-31%). Our findings support the concept that Mb plays a role in modulating skeletal muscle GLU uptake, glycolytic versus oxidative metabolism and total ATP production. Notably, Mb-associated effects appear to be LAC-independent, at least in the C2C12 cell model. Overall, these results are consistent with a growing body of evidence pointing to multiple physiological and regulatory functions for Mb, including cellular fuel trafficking and regulation of mitochondrial function.

articles.title: Reactive oxygen species-mediated cytoskeletal dynamics in osteocytes: The missing link in mechanosensing under Earth and altered gravity.
Free-living daily myofibrillar protein synthesis rates do not differ between vegan and omnivorous diets providing the RDA for protein in older adults.
articles.authors: Benjamin T Wall, Ino van der Heijden, Doaa R Abdelrahman et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Limited data exist on whether vegan diets providing modest protein intakes support daily myofibrillar protein synthesis (MyoPS) rates in older adults OBJECTIVES: To compare daily MyoPS rates, muscle thickness and gene expression in rested and exercised muscle between vegan and isonitrogenous omnivorous diets meeting the protein RDA METHODS: Twenty-two healthy older adults (12 males/10 females; age: 67±4 y; BMI: 25±3 kg/m2) participated in a randomised, parallel-group trial. After 3 days consuming habitual diets, participants consumed a 7-day vegan (VEGAN; n=11) or omnivorous (OMNI; n=11; 69% animal-derived protein) diet providing 0.8 g protein/kg body mass/day. Participants performed three unilateral resistance exercise bouts during the intervention. Deuterated water determined daily MyoPS rates during habitual and intervention periods. Muscle mRNA expression of 48 genes and ultrasound-derived quadriceps muscle thickness were assessed before and after intervention RESULTS: Protein intake decreased by 26% relative to habitual intake (P<0.001). Rested MyoPS rates did not change significantly (OMNI: 1.56±0.32 to 1.37±0.24 %/d; VEGAN: 1.53±0.41 to 1.43±0.24 %/d; P=0.14). Resistance exercise increased MyoPS rates by 17% from habitual (OMNI: 1.74±0.26 %/d; VEGAN: 1.88±0.28 %/d; P=0.0024), resulting in 29% higher rates in exercised than rested muscle during intervention (P<0.0001). MyoPS rates did not differ between diets in rested or exercised muscle at any time point (all P>0.05). Neither muscle thickness nor mRNA expression differed between groups (all P>0.05), although ten genes changed expression following the combined dietary and exercise intervention (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: A feasible vegan diet meeting the protein RDA, despite providing less protein than habitual intakes, supports daily MyoPS rates that do not differ from those supported by an isonitrogenous omnivorous diet in healthy older adults. This trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05985369.

articles.title: Paediatric metabolic syndrome criteria as predictors of early adult metabolic syndrome: findings from the EPITeen cohort.
articles.authors: Tomás Costa, Berta Valente, Milton Severo et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Several definitions of metabolic syndrome (MetS) are used in paediatric populations. This study investigates the predictive capacity of five MetS definitions at age 13 for identifying MetS at age 27 and explores whether adding non-classic variables improves prediction. METHODS: Participants from the EPITeen cohort (n = 815) with valid data on MetS components at ages 13 and 27 were included. At age 13, MetS was defined using Cook, Ferranti, Ford, Agudelo, and International Diabetes Federation (IDF) criteria, and at age 27 using the Alberti consensus. Predictive capacity was estimated using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Performance metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and likelihood ratios were calculated. Non-classic variables were added to the criterion with a higher AUC. RESULTS: At age 13, MetS prevalence ranged from 0.9% (IDF) to 12.5% (Ferranti), and at age 27 it was 3.4%. Ferranti definition had the highest AUC (0.696; 95% CI 0.609-0.784), although not significantly higher than the other criteria. Ferranti was also the least conservative criterion, classifying substantially more adolescents as having MetS (77.4%) but with lower specificity, accuracy, and likelihood ratios than the other criteria. LDL-C was the only non-classic variable that showed a significant improvement in Ferranti's AUC (0.765; 95% CI 0.683-0.846). CONCLUSIONS: Paediatric MetS definitions showed limited ability to predict MetS in early adulthood. Ferranti definition with LDL-C demonstrated the best predictive capacity and, due to its performance metrics, can support targeted preventive public health strategies throughout the life course.

articles.title: Associations of fat mass and fat-free mass accretion in early childhood with body composition and cardiometabolic markers at age 10 years: the Ethiopian iABC birth cohort.
articles.authors: Bikila S Megersa, Suzanne Filteau, Gregers S Andersen et al.
articles.abstract: There is limited evidence on how fat mass (FM) and fat-free mass (FFM) accretion in childhood influence adiposity and cardiometabolic health later in life. We aimed to examine associations of FM and FFM accretion in periods from 0-60 months with body composition, abdominal subcutaneous and visceral fat, and cardiometabolic markers at a mean age of ∼10 years (range: 7-12 years). In the Ethiopian iABC birth cohort, FM and FFM was measured using air-displacement plethysmography. We applied linear spline mixed-effects modeling to estimate FM and FFM accretion during infancy (0-3, 3-6 months) and early childhood (6-48, 48-60 months) in 403 children. The analytical sample ranged from 312 to 307 participants across the outcomes. Multiple linear regression analysis was used to examine associations of FM and FFM accretion in each period with outcomes at age 10 years. FM accretion between 0-3 and 6-48 months was associated with a higher body mass- and FM index, while FFM accretion in all periods was associated with greater height and FFM index at 10 years. FM and FFM accretion from 6-48 months were associated with higher and lower abdominal subcutaneous fat, respectively. Furthermore, FM accretion from 3-6 months was associated with higher systolic blood pressure and glucose levels. FM accretion from 6-48 months was associated with higher fasting insulin, C-peptide, and HOMA-IR, whereas FFM accretion from 6-48 months was associated with lower total and LDL cholesterol. Overall, FM accretion in early infancy and from 6-48 months was linked to adiposity and higher glucose metabolism markers, while FFM accretion from 6-48 months was associated with lower unfavorable lipids, suggesting potential cardiometabolic benefits.

articles.title: Joint associations of EAT-Lancet diet adherence and ambient air-pollution mixtures with respiratory disease risk: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Yemei Chen, Chuanchuan Yu, Liying Zhao et al.
articles.abstract: Whether sustainable dietary patterns and real-world multipollutant exposure are jointly associated with respiratory disease risk remains unclear. We prospectively analysed 64,212 UK Biobank participants with assessment-centre Oxford WebQ data as the primary dietary analysis cohort, with additional analyses incorporating participants with at least one or at least two valid dietary assessments. Adherence to the EAT-Lancet diet was derived from 24-h dietary recall data. For each outcome, an air-pollution mixture score (APS) integrating PM2.5, PM10, PMcoarse, NO2 and NOx was constructed by applying weights estimated from covariate-adjusted weighted quantile sum regression in the corresponding eligible UK Biobank pollution cohort to the dietary analysis cohorts. Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations with incident overall respiratory disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. Each 1-SD higher APS was associated with higher risks of overall respiratory disease (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.10) and COPD (HR 1.09, 95% CI 1.04-1.15), but not asthma. Each 1-point higher EAT-Lancet score was associated with lower risks of overall respiratory disease (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97-0.98) and COPD (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.97), but not asthma. Compared with participants with low EAT-Lancet adherence and high APS, those with high adherence and low APS had lower risks of overall respiratory disease (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66-0.82), COPD (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.54-0.74), and asthma (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68-0.95). Formal interaction tests were not statistically significant in the primary analysis, although COPD interaction estimates were consistently positive across dietary analyses, with the strongest evidence among participants with at least one valid dietary assessment (RERI 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.37). Higher EAT-Lancet adherence and lower multipollutant exposure were jointly associated with lower respiratory disease risks, particularly COPD, suggesting that sustainable dietary patterns may complement population-level air-quality policies.
